messages:
eli: Heads up - started seeing p99 tail spikes on longer (8k+) streams after the recent kernel-selection update. p95 is stable-ish but p99 jumps ~2.5x.

julia: Can you paste the trace + current batcher config? Also which model/kernel did we switch to?

eli: Trace snippet:
```
model: redwood-llama-70b-qlora
kernel: fused-attn-v2
seq_len: 8192
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.64
avg_queue_delay_ms: 18.7
p95_latency_ms: 145
p99_latency_ms: 489
microbatch_tokens: 128
max_batch_tokens: 4096
max_wait_ms: 8
```

eli: Note: kernel v2 reduced avg token time on short seqs but tail seems sensitive to queuing behavior.

max: Looks like avg_queue_delay_ms correlates with p99. Two levers to try:
- lower max_wait_ms (less tail queuing)
- adjust max_batch_tokens / microbatch_tokens to avoid huge single batch assembly

julia: Agree. Also check KV cache eviction behavior - for long contexts we saw more cache churn after kernel change (different KV format). If cache serialization/deserialization is slower, requests could stall waiting for KV loads.

perf-bot: profiling result for last 6h (from /bench/results/1763456700):
```
cpu_util: 36%
gpu_util: 78%
kv_deser_ms_per_request: 6.2
kernel_dispatch_ms: 11.3
queue_wait_ms_p95: 22.4
queue_wait_ms_p99: 98.1
```

anita: Quick A/B suggestion: run two controlled runs for the 8k workload:
A) max_wait_ms=4, max_batch_tokens=2048, microbatch_tokens=64
B) max_wait_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=8192, microbatch_tokens=128
Measure p50/p95/p99 + throughput + cost/sample.

eli: Running A now on shard 3. Command:
```
infra/bench/run.sh --model redwood-llama-70b-qlora --seq 8192 --concurrency 16 --profile --override \"batcher.max_wait_ms=4; batcher.max_batch_tokens=2048; batcher.microbatch_tokens=64\"
```

devops-bot: Deploy started for run A on shard-3. Instance: rwinf-ded-32g-1

max: Also instrument KV cache hits by request prefix length. If hit_ratio drops for >4k prefixes, that's a red flag.

anita: Quick result summary for run A (30m):
- p50: 112ms
- p95: 158ms
- p99: 312ms
- throughput: 92 rps
- cost/sample: +7%
- avg_queue_delay_ms: 9.5
- kv_deser_ms_per_request: 6.1

eli: Run B results (30m):
- p50: 105ms
- p95: 170ms
- p99: 530ms
- throughput: 124 rps
- cost/sample: baseline
- avg_queue_delay_ms: 21.3
- kv_deser_ms_per_request: 6.4

julia: So lowering max_wait_ms reduced p99 substantially at cost of throughput. KV deserialization roughly same, so disk/ser overhead isn't the main cause.

max: Looks like the kernel v2 improves single-token speed but increases variance when batching gets large. Hypothesis: v2 has an internal path that doesn't scale linearly with batch_tokens due to shared workspace growth.

eli: Proposed next steps:
1) Patch batcher to cap per-request contributed tokens to 2048 (ceiling per microbatch) to avoid super-giant batches.
2) Add adaptive max_wait_ms: if queue_wm > 15ms, cut max_wait_ms by 50% for next window.
3) Add metric for kernel_work_size vs internal_workspace_ms to catch non-linear growth.

anita: I'll open a small PR for (1) and (2). Will also add dashboard panel for kernel_work_size.

devops-bot: PR created: git/ops#512 - batcher: per-request token cap + adaptive wait. CI passed.

julia: After PR deploy, let's run a 2h soak on canary and monitor p99 and throughput delta. If p99 stays <350ms and throughput drop <15%, ship.

eli: Thanks - will follow up with soak results. :thumbsup:
